newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks power ahead to another record close.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks power ahead to another record close.

text.p: Swiss shares gained speed after a slow start on Monday to post their fourth consecutive record close due to massive gains in most major banks and pharmaceutical company Roche.
"It was the day of the banks," one dealer said, pointing to a jump of five percent in Swiss Bank Corp and three percent in Credit Suisse.
"The market is likely to keep up the pace," he added.

Dealers said derivatives-related buying, the bright interest rate outlook, technical factors and the continued inflow of liquidity sent shares to new highs. Early Wall Street gains also brightened the horizon.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index advanced 100.5 points, or 1.7 percent, to close at 5,947.0. It touched an all-time high at 5,962.6
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 49.17 points, or 1.34 percent, to 3,729.03.
Bourse volume stood at a robust 3.71 billion Swiss francs.
Banks were sought on the back of expectations that half-year results will be excellent. There was also speculation a U.S. broker had recommended a switch into Swiss from German banks.
Old rumours that some major banks may announce spin-offs or cooperation deals still abounded, dealers observed.
Swiss Bank Corp jumped 21 francs to 429. It declined to comment on market rumours.
UBS and Credit Suisse also posted big gains. Credit Suisse Group was up 6.25 francs to 203.50.
Roche, whose certificates have lagged behind Novartis lately, jumped 355 francs, or 2.6 percent, to 14,005.
One dealer said Roche may now be eyeing a level of 14,300 after clearing 14,000 francs for the first time.
Among the day's losers were Alusuisse, ABB, Ciba, Clariant and Swiss Life. Swiss Life, which has seen big gains since its the first day of trading on July 3, fell eight francs to 573.
